title: The Pickup Window
hook: The drive-thru headset at my job has one rule taped inside it: if someone orders and the lane is empty... don't read the order back.
lines: The drive-thru headset at my job has one rule taped inside it.
If someone orders and the lane is empty... don't read the order back.
The guy who worked nights before me wrote it. Marcus. He walked out in the middle of a shift and never came back.
Three a.m. Rain on the menu board. Then the car sensor chimed.
A soft voice in my ear. Just one, please.
I checked the camera. The lane was empty. Just rain, shining under the lights.
The voice waited. Then the sensor chimed again. And again. Like something was rolling closer... one slow inch at a time.
Then the order printer clicked on by itself. One ticket. One line. My name.
Read it back to me, the voice whispered.
I ripped the headset off. And on the camera... the lane wasn't empty anymore.
A long line of cars stretched out into the dark. Headlights off. Engines silent.
The first one rolled up to my window. Marcus was driving.
He smiled, held up a ticket with my name on it... and said, Order's ready.
